title: Malformed auth cookie can turn an auth failure into a 500
reasoning: cookieValue calls decodeURIComponent directly on user-controlled Cookie header data. If a request includes entity-clickclack-token=% or another malformed percent escape while ENTITY_API_TOKEN is set, decodeURIComponent throws before requireEntityAuth can return the intended 401 response. This makes malformed input produce an internal server error on both proxy route families.
recommendation: Catch URIError in cookieValue and treat the malformed cookie as absent, or use a cookie parser that handles malformed values without throwing.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: proxy.test.ts covers valid cookie, bearer token, missing token, and token stripping paths, but does not send malformed Cookie header values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a proxy route test with ENTITY_API_TOKEN set and Cookie: entity-clickclack-token=% that expects 401 rather than 500.
minimumFixScope: Wrap decodeURIComponent in cookieValue with try/catch and return an empty value for malformed matching cookie values.

history.reasoning: Original evidence path still exists at packages/server/src/clickclack/proxy.ts.
